record.context_brief: General Krylov solvability for Friedrichs-type inverse problems
record.original_question: Given a Hilbert space H, a closed linear operator A acting on H, and a datum g in the range of A, under what assumptions does the inverse problem Af = g admit at least one solution f in the closure of the Krylov subspace K(A, g) = span{g, Ag, A^2 g, ...}? The question also asks for conditions that control whether the Krylov solution is unique and, if Krylov approximants fn are constructed by an abstract truncation algorithm, how quickly fn converges to f.

evidence.quote: QUESTION 1: under what conditions on the (closed) operator A and the vector g ∈ ran A does the inverse problem Af = g admit solution(s) f ∈ K(A, g) ?

The inverse linear problem, in the complex Hilbert space H, Af = g in the unknown f ∈ H and for given densely defined (and possibly closed) linear operator A, and g ∈ ran A ⊂ H – which ensures the existence of solution(s) – is said to be Krylov-solvable if there is a solution f belonging to the closure in H of the Krylov subspace K(A, g) := span{ g, Ag, A^2 g, . . . } ⊂ H associated to A and g.

It is also relevant to investigate in Question 1 the issue of the uniqueness of the Krylov solution, let alone the issue of convergence rate of the Krylov approximants fn → f in one of the abstract algorithms considered.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a complex Hilbert space and let A be a densely defined, closed linear operator on H. For a vector g in the range of A, define the Krylov subspace
  K(A, g) := span{ g, Ag, A^2 g, A^3 g, … } ⊂ H,
where it is assumed that g lies in the intersection of the domains of all powers A^n (n ≥ 0). The inverse linear problem Af = g is said to be Krylov-solvable if there exists a solution f ∈ H lying in the closure of K(A, g) in H.

Determine:
(i) general conditions on the operator A and the datum g ∈ ran A under which the equation Af = g admits at least one solution f belonging to the closure of K(A, g);
(ii) additional conditions which ensure that such a Krylov solution is unique among elements of the closure of K(A, g);
(iii) when an abstract truncation algorithm produces approximants f_n in finite-dimensional truncations of K(A, g), quantitative estimates on the rate at which f_n converges to a Krylov solution f in the norm of H.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2024 perspectives work on Friedrichs systems and Krylov approximation. Partial results exist for bounded operators, compact normal operators, and certain classes of unbounded operators (e.g., Caruso–Michelangeli 2021/2022, Caruso 2022 on compact normal operators), but a complete general characterization for arbitrary closed operators, together with uniqueness criteria and convergence-rate estimates, remains open.

status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for unbounded closed operators.
